entries.why: 2010 and 2014 terms confirmed in IFC's response annexed to the CAO appraisal (Feb 2025). Dropped the 2023 loan terms (water resources risk assessment; noise, vibration and odor monitoring at the waste-to-energy plant): they are on a new loan made about nine years after the 2010-2014 money that built the poultry farm and after the 2018 complaint, and the monitoring clause concerns a different facility. Credit changed to IFC's response, since that is where CAO reproduces these items.

CAO 2021 confirms the eight Critical Path Gaps 'as a condition for financing approval', the pre-investment sediment study requirement and the ESAP recreational-use study; MICI 2020 confirms the IDB action plan (part of the loan contract) required a worker in-migration plan.

CAO 2019 (p.13) confirms IFC's legal agreement required Ficohsa to assess the Tela project against the Performance Standards for its 2013 and 2016 financing and to agree an action plan 'as a condition of additional financing'. The term is specific to this project.
All items confirmed in CAO 2025; 'no-spray zones near water channels' changed to the source's 'non-application zones around drainage and water channels' and 'EU rules' to 'EU principles'.

The only condition-like text is from IFC's Summary of Proposed Investment, a pre-Board summary that says Bankers 'will ensure compliance' with the Performance Standards 'upon implementation' of mitigation measures and that the sponsor 'has agreed' to publish payments; neither is stated as a term the money depended on. The IFC ESRS says the measures are in an Action Plan but does not say it is a loan condition. The CAO assessment confirms only the loan amounts. Owner may wish to know CAO calls the US$50 million loans 'reserve-based', but the source does not say what security that involved, so no 'repay' tag.

CAO investigation confirms the March 2010 investment agreements committing the client to the Performance Standards, the November 2009 ESAP dust limit (average annual PM <=100 mg/Nm3 within 24 months of disbursement) and yearly air monitoring reported to IFC, and the August 2010 waiver request on licence provisions.

Bridge-04 report confirms the October 2013 ESAP and the January 31, 2014 ESMS deadline; Bridge-01 report confirms the ESAP's water quality (WHO standard), structural review and food-hygiene spot-check requirements.

CAO investigation confirms the Action Plan's ESIA requirement (Aug-Nov 2009), the biodiversity assessment as part of it, and the legal agreement clauses (business per the Action Plan; ESIA to IFC before construction).

Facts confirmed in CAO 2020. Kept: the terms sit on IFC's loans to build and refurbish OKKO filling stations, the programme under which the Revutskoho station was planned, though CAO notes a separate developer built it. Fixed the last clause: CAO's 'no specific actions' remark is about the 2013 plan, not both plans (the 2011 plan did include a community fire-drill action).
Confirmed in IRM report paras 33 and annex; the source says the sponsors developed the ESAP 'in accordance with IFC requirements', so 'the lenders' plan' changed to the sponsors' plan.

Facts confirmed in CAO investigation. Kept, because these are the terms on the specific IFC money that flowed to Kamalanga through the Fund (not a bank-wide policy), but added a sentence so readers see the terms bound the Fund, not GMR directly. Owner may still prefer to blank if only terms binding the project company should count.

First sentence confirmed in CAO 2012 appraisal. Dropped the updated post-spill action plan (health impact assessment, drinking water): CAO says it was issued later 'to reflect IFC's recommended actions', i.e. set years after the 2007 investment, so it is not a term of the money at the time.

Facts confirmed in CAO 2010 audit (s.3.5). Fixed who withdrew: IFC management withdrew the proposal and Agrokasa then declined the funding. Owner decision: this money was never invested, so the condition never attached to money that reached the farms.

Facts confirmed (CAO audit s.2.5; SPI 25532: Category C, signed Feb 9, 2007, guarantee exposure not exceeding $50m). 'none' removed: the brief allows it only where a source says no condition was attached, and CAO says only that the Performance Standards 'were not triggered' by the categorization; it does not say the agreements carried no terms. Text kept untagged as reporting (as with manila-water-concessions); owner may blank it instead.

CAO 2008 audit confirms the 1998 onshore oil/gas and thermal power guidelines were specified 'to be referenced in the Loan Agreement' (Oct 30, 2002), the 2002 EAP, the minority-shareholder concern and that the production-sharing agreement does not reference IFC requirements.
Empty in researcher output; nothing to check.

CAO says only that IFC and Mozal assumed failure risk was out of scope 'so long as agreed FTC uptime and point emission targets were being met'. It does not say who agreed the targets, in what document, or that the money depended on them; 'reported against in annual monitoring reports' is not in the audit. No quoted financing clause, so blanked.
CAO 2005 assessment confirms that a breach of the 150 lps release or of the ESMMP 'would be an event of default under the Loan Agreement with IFC'.

Only source is IFC's 2006 Summary of Proposed Investment, which says Rio Tinto 'is committed to' prepare assessments and 'agrees to initiate' a review if critical habitat is found. These are pre-Board statements of the company's intentions, not terms stated as conditions of IFC's money; the cash-call detail describes the investment, not a condition.
